Sanctions on Panamanian Oil & Gas Producers Disrupt Operations Across Canal Zone

Panama City—Sweeping international sanctions targeting Panama’s oil and gas producers have sent shockwaves through the sector, with several major extraction sites in the Canal Zone currently under blockade by authorities. The measures, imposed late Tuesday, have resulted in the immediate suspension of shipments from affected facilities, as enforcement agencies move to seize fuel stocks and halt ongoing exports.

Officials confirmed that at least four sites operated by Energia Istmeña and CanalPetro are now under the control of the National Security Task Force. “We are acting to ensure compliance with the new sanctions regime. Operations at these sites will remain suspended until further notice,” said Interior Minister Luis Guerra at a press conference Wednesday morning.

Trade union representatives voiced alarm over the abrupt halt. “Hundreds of workers have been told to stay home. The uncertainty is growing by the hour,” said Maribel Rodríguez, spokesperson for the Petroleum Workers’ Coalition, who called for an urgent dialogue to address job security.

Industry analysts estimate that more than 60% of Panama’s oil and gas output is currently offline due to the blockades. “Exports have effectively ground to a halt. The longer this persists, the greater the risk to Panama’s position as a regional energy hub,” said Ricardo Ortega, an independent energy consultant.

The Panamanian Oil & Gas Producers Association released a statement urging authorities to seek a diplomatic resolution. “We are deeply concerned about the long-term impact on our industry and workforce,” the statement read. The situation remains tense as negotiations continue.
